 Costco’s Popular Kirkland Whipped Cream Has Just Been Recalled Over Potential Contamination From Cleaning Chemicals 
 Costco’s Popular Kirkland Whipped Cream Has Just Been Recalled Over Potential Contamination From Cleaning Chemicals 
 Here’s how to tell if yours is affected.
 By Jenn Gonick Published: Nov 13, 2026 10:53 AM EST Save Article Share Article dowell // Getty Images We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we back. Why Trust Us? 
 2 min read Key Points 
 Kirkland whipped cream sold at Costco has been voluntarily recalled in 12 states.
 The recalled whipped cream may contain traces of a cleaning chemical.
 Here’s how to tell if yours is affected.
 Many of us can’t imagine a Thanksgiving table without a bunch of pies and some whipped cream, but if you recently bought your can at Costco, you may want to take a second look at the label before spraying a dollop on your slice: Kirkland whipped cream sold at Costco has just been recalled in 12 states.
 According to the notice that the retailer sent to members, the voluntary recall was initiated by Alamance Foods after it “learned that one batch of Kirkland Signature Whipped Cream may contain a small amount of a cleaning chemical.”
 Here’s what you need to know.
 Which products are included in the recall?
 The recall includes one batch of Kirkland whipped cream that was distributed to Costco stores in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Wisconsin. Check your fridge for the following:
 Add Prevention as a preferred source in your Google search results. Use your Google account to add this to your settings. Add to Google settings Kirkland Signature Real Heavy Whipped Cream, 15 oz (425 g), case pack 8CT/3PK 
 Item code: AC50
 Lot: 04/02/2027 (Best If Used By APR/02/27)
 Timestamps on can: 00:35–02:45
 Sold between: October 11, 2026, and October 31, 2026
 More information, including photos of the packaging, can be found in Costco’s announcement .
 What should you do with a recalled product?
 Currently, there have been no reported illnesses associated with the recall, though some Costco members “have reported a chemical smell and taste.” If you do have the recalled whipped cream in your home, don’t eat it. Instead, you can throw it away or return it to your local Costco for a full refund. You can also contact Alamance Foods at customer.care@alamancefood.com with questions about the recall. If you’ve already eaten the recalled whipped cream and have any health concerns, call a doctor right away.
